dedupe_keys.name: performance of compact wireless vibration sensors in the tallwood building full scale shake table test program

description: Shokrullah Sorosh and Tara Hutchinson published measurements comparing Safehub wireless vibration sensors with conventional wired MEMS accelerometers during the TallWood building tests. The programme used a ten-storey mass-timber building, with wireless sensors on floor diaphragms and cold-formed steel exterior and partition walls. The source describes 88 imposed ground motions, with wireless sensors installed during 59 subsets of those motions. These building-scale observations support assessment of building-response monitoring and sensor performance under shaking. Exact sampling intervals and file formats remain unknown in the inspected metadata. DesignSafe provides public repository access at no stated charge under Open Data Commons Attribution. Sensor accuracy and the underlying time series were not independently checked. The project cites the wider TallWood test dataset as a related source; the catalogue also links the DesignSafe Data Depot repository.
